bib.title: CLaRa: Bridging Retrieval and Generation with Continuous Latent Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "CLaRa: Bridging Retrieval and Generation with Continuous Latent Reasoning", Jie He (first author; Apple / Univ. of Edinburgh), Richard He Bai, Sinead Williamson, Jeff Z. Pan, Navdeep Jaitly, Yizhe Zhang. arXiv:2511.18659v3 (cs.CL), dated 5/9 Feb 2026. No venue is stated, so call it preprint, 2025 (v1 Nov 2025). Code: github.com/apple/ml-clara.

COVERAGE: 124,421 chars extracted from all 40 pages. I read the main text (pp. 1-10), the appendix A derivation, B setup, Tables 5-7, 10-17 and the C-H text in full. I skimmed the reference list (it is only for origins) and the tail of Table 6 and Table 18 (paraphrase examples). Nothing was garbled. Figures were not rendered; I used the caption text only. The paper has no explicit "Limitations" section. The limits below are inferred from the Impact Statement and the tables.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Soft-compressed documents plus a jointly trained reranker nearly match a text-based jointly trained system at 16x compression.
 number: Table 2 averages for CLaRa-Mistral-7B, instruction-initialized, Normal setting, 16x: F1 40.30 and EM 31.65. DRO-Mistral-7B (raw text, 1x): F1 41.96 and EM 36.56. NQ F1 50.89 against DRO's 51.01.
 setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 with LoRA. Wikipedia-2021, BGE-large-en-v1.5 top-20 candidates, CLaRa picks the top-5. Full dev sets of NQ, HotpotQA, MuSiQue and 2Wiki. Baseline numbers are copied from the DRO paper (marked *), not re-run.
 quote: "Overall, our method achieves comparable performance while reducing the required context length by 16×."
 where: Table 2, p. 8.
 CAUTION: the abstract says CLaRa outperforms text-based fine-tuned baselines, and the text says "CLaRa-Mistral-7B with 16x surpasses the text-based DRO-Mistral-7B, improving F1 from 51.01→51.41 on NQ and 43.65→47.18 on 2Wiki". Table 2 does not support the NQ half. The 16x NQ F1 is 50.89, and 51.41 is the 128x row in Table 6. DRO also wins on average F1 and on EM everywhere, so "comparable, not better" is the safe wording. The 2Wiki figure of 47.18 is the 4x row, not 16x.
 
2. Compressed representations match or beat uncompressed raw-text input at the same retrieval.
 number: SCP-Mistral-7B at 4x averages 39.86 CEM against 37.67 for raw text. At 16x it averages 38.96. Phi4-mini at 4x averages 37.40 against 32.28.
 setup: Table 1 Normal setting, BGE top-5, CEM (answer contained in output). Four QA sets.
 quote: "Surprisingly, our model exceeds the text-based baseline using uncompressed documents, with average gains of 2.36% on Mistral-7B and 6.36% on Phi-4-min."
 where: p. 7-8, Table 1 and Table 5.
 The authors' explanation is untested: "This may be because the compressed representations filter out irrelevant content". Under the Oracle setting the benefit fades. Mistral at 16x averages 63.90 against 64.24 for raw text, and falls to 61.53 at 32x.

3. Hard versus soft compression and the best soft baseline.
 number: Gains of 1.13% (Normal) and 5.35% (Oracle) over PISCO. Gains of 5.37% and 17.31% over LLMLingua-2 (4x).
 quote: "Compared to the best soft compression model PISCO, our model achieves average gains of 1.13% (Normal) and 5.35% (Oracle); over the hard compression baseline LLMLingual-2, improvements reach 5.37% and 17.31%"
 where: p. 7. The Normal gain over PISCO is small, 38.96 against 37.83 at 16x.

4. Retrieval trained only from the generator's next-token loss (no relevance labels) beats a supervised reranker.
 number: HotpotQA Recall@5 of 96.21% at 4x against 85.93% for BGE-Reranker (+10.28).
 setup: Oracle setting (gold doc guaranteed in the 20 candidates), Mistral-7B, pretraining-initialized. Table 7.
 quote: "On HotpotQA (compression ratio 4), it achieves a Recall@5 of 96.21%, exceeding the strongest supervised baseline BGE-Reranker (85.93%) by +10.28%."
 where: p. 9, Table 7 p. 20.
 CAUTION: the headline comparison is to the off-the-shelf BGE-Reranker. The authors' own contrastively trained Sup-Mistral-7B gets 82.84 at the same cell, and 85.02 on 2Wiki against CLaRa's 79.13. On NQ, CLaRa is only 76.38 against 74.96. The win is HotpotQA-specific, and it drops to 87.85 at 16x. Instruction-initialized CLaRa is worse than Sup on several sets (Recall@5 on NQ at 4x: 69.82 against 71.96). Phi4-mini CLaRa is very weak at low compression (NQ Recall@5 of 44.61 at 4x). The comparison is on a candidate set of 20, one document at a time, and no seeds are reported.

5. Differentiable top-k is the mechanism for joint training.
 quote: "Z=Z hard + (Z soft −SG(Z soft))" (Eq. 3.5). A straight-through estimator takes a hard argmax in the forward pass and a softmax gradient in the backward pass. The paper contrasts this with RL-based sampling (RAG-DDR), which it calls unstable and inefficient.
 number: none. Training uses cosine score s_i = cos(q, M_i), top-k = 5 from 20 candidates, one epoch, end-to-end LR 5e-6, batch 32.
 where: p. 5-6, Table 10 (p. 21).

6. Pretraining (SCP) data composition matters. QA plus paraphrase beats either alone.
 number: Oracle, 32x, Mistral average 54.39 (no pretrain), 58.90 (SimpleQA), 60.64 (Para), 61.53 (SimpleQA+ComplexQA+Para, +7.14). Phi4-mini 52.39 to 56.38 (+3.99).
 setup: Table 3, instruction-tuned after pretraining. 2M Wikipedia-2021 documents with Qwen-32B-generated QA and paraphrase, verified over up to 10 regeneration rounds.
 quote: "SimpleQA+ComplexQA+Para 73.77+3.7669.51+8.3838.31+9.3164.54+7.1161.53+7.14"
 where: Table 3, p. 9.
 Data scale: 0.5M to 1M documents helps (Oracle Mistral 54.98 to 61.46); 2M adds nothing (61.53). Table 11, p. 24.
 Manual check: "Only 21 instances exhibited mild hallucinations" of 600 sampled, judged by one author (p. 24).

7. The compression ratio degrades gracefully, then falls off sharply with retrieval quality.
 number: Normal setting, Mistral SCP average runs 39.86 (4x), 38.96 (16x), 38.82 (32x), 38.39 (64x), 37.85 (128x), 37.38 (256x). Oracle runs 66.76 down to 52.86 at 256x. Phi4-mini collapses faster: Oracle 62.61 at 4x to 45.40 at 256x.
 where: Table 5, p. 18. Chunk size 256 tokens, memory tokens = 256/ratio.
 quote: "While performance declines at extreme compression (beyond 32× in Oracle), the drop remains moderate under Normal conditions due to weaker document relevance."
 In the end-to-end Table 2, 4x is worse than 16x/32x, which the authors only guess is because "4× might be harder to optim w/ NTP".

8. A trainable query encoder drives the end-to-end gain, and a compressor-initialized query reasoner beats a random one.
 number: Oracle 32x HotpotQA F1 52.54 (generator only) to 70.91 (query reasoner + generator). Random init to compressor init: 66.84 to 70.91 (HotpotQA), 62.68 to 66.32 (2Wiki).
 where: Tables 13-14, p. 26-27.
 Fine-tuning the compressor too gave under 2.0 points on average at instruction tuning ("only marginal improvements").

9. Efficiency.
 number: Decoding takes 502-533 ms with compressed inputs against 1290.57 ms for raw text on Mistral-7B (about 40%). On Phi4-mini it is 342-360 ms against 870.29 ms.
 quote: "decoding with compressed representations takes only about 40% of the time required when using full-text documents."
 setup: single H100 80GB, 20 candidates compressed to 5. Compression takes 835-1092 ms per query on Mistral and is offline-able, so excluded from latency (Table 15, p. 28). Query encoding takes about 90-100 ms.
 CAUTION: the "offline compression" claim only holds if the corpus is static and re-compression is not counted. Storage of the memory-token vectors is not reported.

10. Fidelity and grounding.
 number: Reconstruction BERTScore stays at about 90 at all ratios (89.19 at 256x, seen data). Entity preservation falls from 54.78 (4x) to 42.12 (256x) on seen data, and from 60.04 to 52.38 on unseen data.
 where: Table 16, p. 29.
 Instruction-tuned models lose factual correctness (RAGAS, GPT-4o-mini judge). The authors suspect longer, more elaborate answers, and the reason is untested. Pretraining-initialized end-to-end faithfulness runs 81.57 at 4x down to 64.74 at 256x on NQ Normal (Table 17).

11. The pretraining-initialized checkpoint retrieves better, but the instruction-initialized one answers better.
 quote: "instruction tuning, while improving answer generation, biases the model toward localized evidence at the cost of global semantics crucial for retrieval."
 where: p. 9. This is a trade-off, and it is explained by the authors' reading, not by an ablation.

12. Auxiliary MSE alignment loss is a small gain.
 number: 0.3-0.6 average points, with mixed sign per dataset (NQ -0.88 at 32x).
 quote: "leads to a modest (0.3–0.6 points on average) but consistent improvement across datasets"
 where: Table 4, p. 9. Loss weight λ = 0.1.

13. Qualitative: the query embedding decodes (logit lens, top-50) to tokens absent from the question, such as "NFL" and "Oklahoma" for the Ivory Lee Brown question. This is anecdotal (one case), p. 6, Fig. 4.

14. Gradient theory (App. A). In the non-shared case ∂p(y|x,d)/∂s = 0, so only the "probability path" gradient flows. In the shared-representation case a second "representation/generation path" term appears: (p(r|x)p(y|x,r)/τ)·π_d·gᵀ(z_d − r). This is the paper's "theoretical justification". It relies on a stated simplifying assumption (per-document conditionals), and it says nothing about whether training converges to better retrieval.

LIMITS
- The authors concede the compressor is "pretrained primarily on Wikipedia data, which may reflect existing coverage biases", and that diverse domain-specific data is future work (Impact Statement, p. 11).
- Only Wikipedia-2021 and four QA benchmarks (NQ, HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2Wiki). Only two backbones (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Phi-4-mini-instruct). Short-answer metrics (EM, F1, CEM). Single run, no seeds or variance reported.
- The baselines in Table 2 are copied from the DRO paper, so they are not run under identical conditions.
- Weak gains in the Normal (realistic) setting. Absolute F1 on MuSiQue is 15-18, and EM is well below F1 (31.65 against 40.30 average). The large wins (F1 above 75) come from the Oracle setting, which assumes the gold document is in the candidates.
- Phi4-mini is much worse (end-to-end Normal NQ F1 about 30-42), so the method is capacity-sensitive.
- The cost of compressing the whole corpus once, and the storage of the vectors, are not quantified. Re-indexing is needed if the compressor changes (the compressor is frozen during end-to-end training to avoid this).
- Requires white-box weights and LoRA training, so it cannot be used with API-only generators.
- The Case Study and the "filters irrelevant content" explanation are anecdotal.
- Dated: Mistral-7B v0.2 and Wikipedia-2021 baselines. No long-context or agentic evaluation.

BUILDS ON
- PISCO (Louis et al., ACL Findings 2025): memory tokens plus LoRA adapters, sequence-level distillation.
- COCOM (Rau et al., 2025): instruction-tuning data (453k questions).
- xRAG (Cheng et al., NeurIPS 2024), AutoCompressor (Chevalier et al., EMNLP 2023), PCC (Dai et al., ACL 2025), LLMLingua-2 (Pan et al., ACL Findings 2024), gist tokens (Mu et al., NeurIPS 2023), ICAE (Ge et al., ICLR 2024).
- DRO (Shi et al., 2025): the training recipe (top-20 candidates, top-5) and the baseline numbers.
- RAG-DDR (Li et al., ICLR 2025): the RL-style baseline.
- Straight-through estimator (Bengio, Léonard and Courville, 2013).
- Logit lens (nostalgebraist, 2020).
- OSCAR (Louis et al., 2025b): the closest related work, query-aware online compression.
- Gumbel Reranking (Huang et al., ACL 2025).
- RECOMP (Xu et al., 2024): a baseline in Table 2 (numbers copied from DRO).
- Atlas (Izacard et al., 2023) for the Wikipedia-2021 corpus.

CODE: No code. Key equations: Eq. 2.2 L_total = L_CE + λ·L_MSE (p. 4); Eq. 3.1 s_i = cos(q, M_i); Eq. 3.3-3.5 soft/hard/straight-through selection (p. 5); Eq. 3.2 the end-to-end language-modelling loss. Algorithm 1 is cited in the appendix, but I did not read it separately.

FIGURES (captions only, not rendered)
- Fig. 1 (p. 2): the whole pipeline (compressor pretraining, offline compression, query reasoner, training and inference) plus a decoded-query example. This is the single most useful diagram.
- Fig. 2 (p. 3): SCP data synthesis (QA, paraphrase, verify, regenerate) and compressor training.
- Fig. 3 (p. 4): the end-to-end training diagram with the top-k straight-through path.
- Fig. 4 (p. 6): logit-lens decoding of a query embedding.
- Fig. 5 (p. 8): Recall@1/3/5 for NQ and HotpotQA across supervised and weakly supervised rerankers.
- Fig. 7 (p. 25) is training curves, Fig. 8 (p. 27) is the effect of top-k at test time, and Fig. 9 (p. 30) is a t-SNE with and without MSE.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table text had extraction glitches (columns merged, "+/-" deltas fused with values). A few numbers in the prose do not match the tables (see claim 1). Table 6 and Table 18 tails were only skimmed.

NOTE-FIT (grep on the three notes)
- A grep of 11, 05 and 06 for clara, pisco, xrag, "soft compress", latent, memory token, straight-through, differentiable and "end-to-end" finds no CLaRa, PISCO, xRAG or soft-compression content. So the note does not say any of this yet.
- 05-chunking-query-parsing-and-reranking.md line 548 ("Compress after reranking, and let the compressor return nothing") covers RECOMP only, as a text-level compressor with Flan-UL2 20B. CLaRa's Table 2 lists RECOMP* as a 1x row (copied from DRO: NQ F1 42.67, HotpotQA 42.72 under the Normal setting). That is a sharpens citation for RECOMP only.
- 06-generation-for-rag.md line 242 (the compression table) covers LLMLingua only. CLaRa's Table 1 adds LLMLingua-2 at 4x (average CEM 34.49, against 39.86 for SCP at 4x) and a soft-compression family (xRAG, PISCO, COCOM, PCC), which is a natural new row. It extends the "hard compression" paragraph with the soft-compression counterpart.
- Strongest fit: 06 (generation for RAG, context compression: soft memory-token compression at 16x with a 60% decoding-time cut, Claims 2, 7, 9). Second: 05 (reranking), where the weakly supervised, label-free reranker (Claim 4) goes next to the RECOMP paragraph at line 548.
- 11-retrieval-improvements.md is a weak home. Its joint-training coverage is MMOA-RAG, with PPO and a frozen retriever, at about line 379. CLaRa is the contrast case there: differentiable top-k replaces RL, but it needs white-box LoRA training. It is not a recipe for the Tallybook project in that note.
- Practical triage for the course: cite CLaRa as a sharpens in 05 (RECOMP row) and 06 (compression table), and mention it at line 379 of 11 with the 16x "comparable, not better" wording. Do not quote the 51.01 to 51.41 improvement.
